definitions.explanation: A legal document specifying how a person's property and affairs should be handled after death. This reading is the formal legal term, as opposed to the more general ゆいごん.

examples.japanese: {遺言|いごん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作成|さくせい}する→作成する：25378_sakuseisuru⟧。
{遺言|いごん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{内容|ないよう}→内容：01482_naiyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{公開|こうかい}→公開：11665_koukai⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The contents of the will were made public.

examples.japanese: ⟦{弁護士|べんごし}→弁護士：03150_bengoshi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{依頼|いらい}して→依頼する：21376_irai⟧⟦{正式|せいしき}→正式：03376_seishiki⟧な{遺言|いごん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作成|さくせい}して→作成する：25378_sakuseisuru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I had a lawyer draft a formal will for me.

notes: The reading いごん is the standard legal term used in courts, law offices, and official documents. The more common reading {遺言|ゆいごん} is used in everyday speech and has a broader meaning that includes dying wishes and last words. Legal types include {自筆証書遺言|じひつしょうしょいごん} (holographic will), {公正証書遺言|こうせいしょうしょいごん} (notarial will), and {秘密証書遺言|ひみつしょうしょいごん} (sealed will). Common collocations: {遺言|いごん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{残|のこ}す→残す：01975_nokosu⟧ (to leave a will), {遺言|いごん}⟦{書|しょ}→〜書：28467_sho⟧ (written will).
